title: Project: student records
learningGoals: combine a vector, a lambda and algorithms

youtube.title: C++ Project: Student Records Program | C++ Programming EP 88
youtube.description: In this episode you will design a small class, combine a vector, a lambda and algorithms and write a const correct class, with Xecxec the crab. 0:00 Intro · 0:16 Project: student records · 0:46 The Roster class · 1:34 Class design · 2:04 Second program · 3:04 Recap · 3:34 Bug of the Day · 4:22 Challenge · 4:42 Next episode

thumbnail.pose: Xecxec next to a crab with a clipboard and a stack of report cards

scenes.animation: Tomato title card: EP sticker thuds in, title stamps with a whoosh, Xecxec scuttles in and waves; thud, whoosh, claw-click, sting
scenes.narration: Today we build a small project. A roster class holds student marks. It can add a student, print a ranking, and find the best student.

scenes.onScreen: "Project: student records": numbered lines (1. One class owns the data; 2. Methods that only read are const; 3. Use library algorithms inside the class) and an analogy card: a teacher with a register: add a student, ask for the average
scenes.animation: Lines spring in one by one with a pop; the analogy card slides in from the right
scenes.narration: A good class owns its data and hides it. It offers a few clear methods. Methods that only read the data are marked const. We use a vector to store students, a lambda to sort them, and an optional for the best student.
points: Methods that only read are const
Use library algorithms inside the class

analogy.title: Project: student records
analogy.body: A teacher with a register: add a student, ask for the average

scenes.onScreen: roster.cpp: a roster adds students, ranks them and computes the average
scenes.animation: Code types in with key-tick; butter [HL n] highlight sweeps line by line with marker-swipe; explanation card on the right
scenes.narration: [HL 15] Add stores one student at the back of the vector. [HL 19] Average only reads the data, so it is const. [HL 24] If the roster is empty, we return zero, and we never divide by zero. [HL 28] Print ranking works on a copy, so the original order does not change. [HL 29] The lambda puts the highest marks first. [HL 35] The vector is private. Only the class can change it. [HL 41] Main adds three students. [HL 44] The ranking is Asha ninety-one, Mia eighty-five, Ravi seventy-eight. [HL 45] The average is eighty-four point seven.

scenes.onScreen: a table of the members of Roster
scenes.animation: Table rows slide in one by one; the row the narrator mentions glows butter
scenes.narration: The data is private. The add method changes the roster, so it is not const. Average and print ranking only read the data, so both are const.

diagram.caption: a table of the members of Roster

scenes.onScreen: best.cpp: best returns an optional student
scenes.animation: Second program or a twist on the first; [HL n] and [TRACK name=value] cues drive the variable tracker; output panel fills line by line with a ding per line
scenes.narration: [HL 19] Best returns an optional, because an empty roster has no best student. [HL 21] For an empty roster, it returns nullopt. [HL 23] Max element finds the student with the highest marks. [HL 24] The lambda says that a is smaller than b when a has fewer marks. [HL 34] The first call is on an empty roster, so it prints zero. [HL 38] After two adds, the optional holds a value. The output is Asha ninety-one.

scenes.animation: Dark-blue terminal: the compile command types with key-tick, the run command types, output prints in mint with a ding
scenes.narration: Save the file as best dot cpp. Compile it with g plus plus. Then run the program. The program prints the ranking and the average, then zero, and then Asha ninety-one.

scenes.animation: Recap lines tick in one by one with a pop; Xecxec nods after each tick
scenes.narration: Let us recap. One. A class owns its data and keeps it private. Two. Mark read only methods const. Three. A lambda gives sort its rule. Four. Optional says that a result may not exist. Pause the video. Say these ideas out loud, one time, slowly.
points: A class owns its data and keeps it private.
A lambda gives sort its rule.
Optional says that a result may not exist.

scenes.onScreen: BUG OF THE DAY: A const object calls a non const method
scenes.animation: Butter banner drops in with a buzzer; wrong code shakes; the g++ error lines appear in tomato; the fix slides in and the terminal turns mint with a ding
scenes.narration: Bug of the Day. The function gets a const reference, and calls average. The compiler says this discards qualifiers. Average does not change the object, so mark it const.

scenes.onScreen: Why did the roster stay calm? Everything inside it was in order.
scenes.animation: Full tomato screen, card flips in with a rimshot, Xecxec snaps his claw
scenes.narration: Why did the roster stay calm? Everything inside it was in order.

scenes.onScreen: Task card: add a method to find a student
scenes.animation: Task card pops in; checklist ticks with a pop; Xecxec holds a tiny pen
scenes.narration: Your challenge: Add a method that takes a name and returns the marks of that student as an optional. Write your answer in the comments.

scenes.onScreen: Next: EP 89 · Common mistakes and exam questions
scenes.animation: Next-episode card slides up with a whoosh; right side stays empty for end-screen elements; sign-off text types in
scenes.narration: Next time: common mistakes and exam questions. Keep coding, says Xecxec!

bug.error:
Compiler output (exactly as g++ prints it):

constbug.cpp: In function 'void show(const Roster&)':
constbug.cpp:21:22: error: passing 'const Roster' as 'this' argument discards qualifiers [-fpermissive]
   21 |     cout << r.average() << endl;
      |             ~~~~~~~~~^~
constbug.cpp:8:12: note:   in call to 'double Roster::average()'
    8 |     double average() {
bug.why: A const reference may call only const methods. Add const after the parameter list of every method that does not change the object.

pun: "Why did the roster stay calm? Everything inside it was in order."
challenge: Add a method that takes a name and returns the marks of that student as an optional.
challengeAnswer: Loop over the students. If the name matches, return the marks. After the loop, return nullopt.
